anomalies.obs: On page 1 the TACH pull-up R6 (10K) is connected between the VCC net and the TACH net. TACH is the fan tachometer sense line and is routed straight to the MCU tach input (U2 pin3 / U3 pin2). VCC is the unregulated input rail (it is the input of the LM1117-5.0 regulator U1, whose output is the separate +5V net that powers the MCUs), so VCC is above the MCU's 5V supply.
anomalies.expected: An open-collector tachometer pull-up feeding a 5V MCU input must be tied to the MCU's own supply rail (+5V), not to the higher unregulated fan/input rail VCC, otherwise the pin is pulled above VCC+0.5V absolute maximum.

evidence.quote: Page 1: R6 10K drawn between 'VCC' (top) and 'TACH' (right); TACH net also on U2 pin3 / U3 pin2
Page 2: U1 'LM1117-5.0' with VI on 'VCC' and VO on '+5V'; U2/U3 pin8 on '+5V'

anomalies.impact: When the fan tach output is high-impedance (off), R6 pulls the MCU tach input to VCC (>5V), exceeding the ATtiny pin absolute-maximum rating and risking damage or latching, and giving wrong logic thresholds on the speed-sense line.

parsed.summary: The fan tachometer pull-up R6 ties the sense line to the unregulated VCC rail instead of the MCU's +5V rail (VCC is the LM1117-5.0 input, hence higher than +5V), over-volting the MCU tach input; this is the one deviation supported by the drawing.
